points.description: States that global variables have file scope, i.e. they are declared outside all functions/blocks and are accessible from the point of declaration to the end of the file (translation unit), so usable by all functions in that file.
points.partial_credit: Award 2.5 only if the student gives clearly more than half of this precisely, e.g. says they are accessible by all functions in the program/file but does not use the term 'file scope'; vague answers such as 'everywhere' earn 0.

rubric.notes: Full marks only if the answer says file scope (accessible throughout the file/translation unit, declared outside any function). Part marks only for a precise partial statement, such as accessible to all functions without naming file scope. Wrong scopes (local, block, function scope) or vague answers such as 'global' or 'everywhere' earn nothing; stating a wrong scope alongside the right one also earns nothing.
